Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph S. 20L MS. MARYLOU S. MONTEFALCON MLGOO Municipality of Bansalan Province of Davao del Sur Dear MLGOO Montefalcon: 14 OCT 2019 This has reference to your letter dated 17 June 2019, requesting the Department's opinion on the legality of the appointments issued by your outgoing Acting Mayor Edwin G. Reyes of Bansalan, Davao del Sur. Perusal of your letter appears that the "appointment" you are mentioning pertains to "hiring of Job Orders". It must be emphasized that hiring of Job Orders is not the same with the appointment of employees as contemplated in Section of the Local Government Code (LGC). At the outset, this Department has been very consistent in its previous legal opinions that the Vice-Mayor acting as Acting Mayor can perform all the duties and powers pertaining to the Office of the Mayor, except the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. Thus, if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days, the Acting Mayor may already proceed to exercise such functions so as not to impair the delivery of vital public service. The appointment, suspension and dismissal of employees mentioned herein pertains to plantilla positions. The Department anchored its position in Section 46(a) of the Local Government Code (LGC). It is further emphasized that nowhere in the language of said provision can it be found that such power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees can only be exercised after the lapse of thirty working days. Therefore, if it is apparent that the incapacity, as in the case of legal incapacity due to suspension from office, exceeds thirty working days, the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss may already be exercised by the acting mayor immediately upon his or her temporary assumption to that office2 1 SECTION 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. - (a) When the govemor, city or municipal Mayor, or Punong Barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor, city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking Sangguniang Barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. 2 DILG Legal Opinion No. 023-01, dated 16 April 2001

On the other hand, as to Job Order Contracts, the LGC provided no time limit in hiring the same. Hence, Section 46(a) of the LGC is not applicable because it only refers to the hiring of plantilla positions. Job Order Contracts can be hired by the Acting Mayor anytime pursuant to Section 77 of the LGC, to wit: "SECTION 77. Responsibility for Human Resources and Development. - The chief executive of every local government unit shall be responsible for human resources and development in his unit and shall take all personnel actions in accordance with the Constitutional provisions on civil service, pertinent laws, and rules and regulations thereon, including such policies, guidelines and standards as the Civil Service Commission may establish: Provided, That the local chief executive may employ emergency or casual employees or laborers paid on a daily wage or piecework basis and hired through job orders for local projects authorized by the Sanggunian concerned, without need of approval or attestation by the Civil Service Commission: Provided, further, That the period of employment of emergency or casual laborers as provided in this Section shall not exceed six (6) months. " (Emphasis ours) Since the Acting Mayor has the power to perform all the duties and powers pertaining to the Office of the Mayor, the Acting Mayor, being the local chief executive, albeit in an acting capacity, can also hire Job Orders pursuant to Section 77 of the I-GC, aside from appointment of employees (plantilla position) pursuant to Section 46(a) of the LGC. Accordingly, this Department finds that the hiring of job orders of the outgoing Acting Mayor is well within his power pursuant to Section 77 of the LGC. However, emphasis is made that the period of hiring job orders shall not exceed six (6) months as provided in the afore-quoted law. cc: We hope we have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: MARIVE C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary Dir. Alex C. Roldan, CESO V Regional Director DILG-Region X1 Ls/90b
